passages.note: Bill status/history page; does not name Livingston, so it cannot establish his own act -- used only to confirm the instrument and its title change from permanent school fund to tipped workers; wages.
House Third Reading vote; Livingston voted Y on a tipped-wage subminimum exemption, a narrower clause than the ladder's general wage-floor question.

passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked.
passages.note: Operative text of the House-engrossed SCR1040: creates a tip-credit subminimum wage, not a change to the general wage floor the ladder's rungs describe.

rows.reasoning: Livingston voted Yea on SCR1040 (2024), a House-passed resolution allowing employers to pay tipped workers up to twenty-five percent less than the minimum wage when tips make up the difference. Per the topic annex, a tipped-wage subminimum exemption speaks to the wage-floor question but does not state the general rule the rungs describe, such as 'raise the wage floor' or 'hold the wage floor at its current level', so it is direction-only rather than chair-shaped.
needs_source: Livingston's own statement(s) on the general minimum wage question, not limited to the tipped-worker subminimum
